Try itSpeed profile, step 1: a curve caps the speed
Lateral acceleration
  • On a circle of radius \(R\) at speed \(v\), the AV accelerates toward the circle's center by \(v^{2}/R\) (m/s2).
  • The tires must push the AV sideways that hard; the faster or the tighter the curve, the harder.

We cap it at \(a_{\text{lat}} = 2.0\) m/s2 (chosen; the controller node's a_lat, a cap the node applies itself).

A curve caps the speed
  • the sideways acceleration stays within the limit: \(v^{2}/R \le a_{\text{lat}}\)
  • so the highest speed on a curve of radius \(R\) is \(v = \sqrt{a_{\text{lat}} R}\)
  • as \(R = 1/\kappa\): \(v = \sqrt{a_{\text{lat}} / \kappa}\)
\(a_{\text{lat}}\) captry it

    These caps are the speed limit at each point, the dashed line in the next panel.
